open_theses.question: How many advanced AI accelerators will Huawei, together with its chipmaking partner SMIC, produce in calendar 2026 (combined Huawei-designed Ascend output: 910B, 910C and the new 950PR line)?

open_theses.question: What will the CPU-to-GPU attach ratio in AI inference workloads be in 2026, as Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan says it is beginning to shift from 1 CPU to 8 GPUs toward 1 CPU to 1 GPU?
open_theses.outcome: The reported CPU:GPU ratio for AI inference workloads in 2026, and whether it has moved materially from 1:8 toward 1:1.

open_theses.question: Will NVIDIA's Vera Rubin next-generation AI chip platform, the product line that carries its data center value, begin shipping by a check date (end of calendar 2026)?
open_theses.outcome: Confirmation that first Vera Rubin shipments have begun, versus slipping into 2027 or later.

open_theses.question: How many advanced AI accelerators will Huawei, together with its chipmaking partner SMIC, produce in calendar 2026 (combined Huawei-designed Ascend output: 910B, 910C and the new 950PR line)?
open_theses.outcome: The combined 2026 output of Huawei-designed AI chips manufactured at SMIC, in units, measured against the contested estimates in circulation (Nvidia's report: SMIC above 700,000 Ascend 910C by end-2026 at a 50,000-per-month run rate and several million 910B in 2027; Commerce Secretary Lutnick: 200,000 advanced chips for 2025; Chris McGuire: 800,000 910C in 2025, 2 million in 2026 and 4 million in 2027 as stress cases).

open_theses.question: Will Nvidia actually resume selling H200 AI chips into China by Nvidia's FY2027 year-end — i.e., will Beijing permit Chinese commercial users to buy the chips the U.S. cleared for export in December 2025?
open_theses.outcome: Whether H200 sales to Chinese customers take place (China data-center revenue returning above zero) versus Beijing keeping Nvidia locked out despite the U.S. approval.

open_theses.question: What will the big four AI hyperscalers' combined data center capital expenditures be in calendar 2027, and will they approach the roughly $1 trillion level Nvidia projects for next year?
open_theses.outcome: The combined 2027 data center capex of the big four AI hyperscalers, measured against Nvidia's ~$1 trillion projection and the 2026 level of ~$650 billion.

open_theses.question: Will Nvidia's Kyber NVL144 rack-scale architecture — the rack system that houses its Rubin Ultra generation, the generation after Vera Rubin — reach first shipments in 2028, after SemiAnalysis reported the program has slipped more than 12 months from a planned 2027 debut?
open_theses.outcome: First shipments of the Kyber NVL144 rack system (Rubin Ultra generation) in 2028 versus the original 2027 schedule, and whether the larger NVL576 multi-rack system ships in volume at all.

new_theses.question: What will contract prices for AI-relevant memory (DDR5/DRAM, LPDDR5X, 3D NAND and HBM) do over calendar 2026, the input cost that now makes up roughly a quarter to 30% of Nvidia's Vera Rubin rack bill of materials?
new_theses.outcome: The direction and magnitude of 2026 memory contract pricing (DRAM/DDR5, LPDDR5X, 3D NAND, HBM) after the reported 435% jump in memory content per Nvidia AI rack, and whether memory inflation continues or eases.
new_theses.period: Calendar 2026, with emphasis on H2 2026 — set because the item frames AI infrastructure budgeting for the second half of 2026 and beyond, reports memory supply tight and contract DDR5 pricing climbing sharply, and gives no specific release date of its own.
